segments.arabic: [3] حدثنا يحيى بن بكير قال: حدثنا الليث عن عقيل عن ابن شهاب عن عروة بن الزبير عن عائشة أم المؤمنين أنها قالت
segments.english: Yahya ibn Bukayr related to us: al-Layth related to us, from ‘Uqayl, from Ibn Shihab, from ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ‘A’ishah, the Mother of the Believers, who said:

segments.arabic: أول ما بدئ به رسول الله ﷺ من الوحي الرؤيا الصالحة في النوم فكان لا يرى رؤيا إلا جاءت مثل فلق الصبح
segments.english: The first revelation with which the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, began was good dreams during sleep. He would see no dream except that it came like the break of dawn.

segments.arabic: ثم حبب إليه الخلاء وكان يخلو بغار حراء فيتحنث فيه وهو التعبد الليالي ذوات العدد قبل أن ينزع إلى أهله ويتزود لذلك ثم يرجع إلى خديجة فيتزود لمثلها حتى جاءه الحق وهو في غار حراء
segments.english: Then solitude was made dear to him. He used to withdraw to the cave of Hira and devote himself there to worship—which is the meaning of tahannuth—for a number of nights before returning to his family. He would take provisions for that, then return to Khadijah and take provisions for a similar stay, until the truth came to him while he was in the cave of Hira.

segments.arabic: فجاءه الملك، فقال اقرأ قال: ما أنا بقارئ قال: فأخذني فغطني حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم أرسلني، فقال اقرأ قلت: ما أنا بقارئ فأخذني فغطني الثانية حتى بلغ مني الجهد ثم أرسلني، فقال اقرأ فقلت: ما أنا بقارئ فأخذني فغطني الثالثة ثم أرسلني، فقال { اقرأ باسم ربك الذي خلق. خلق الإنسان من علق اقرأ وربك الأكرم }
segments.english: The angel came to him and said, “Read.” He said, “I cannot read.” He said: “He took hold of me and pressed me until I reached the limit of my strength. Then he released me and said, ‘Read.’ I said, ‘I cannot read.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a second time until I reached the limit of my strength. Then he released me and said, ‘Read.’ I said, ‘I cannot read.’ He took hold of me and pressed me a third time. Then he released me and said: ‘Read in the name of your Lord who created. He created the human being from a clot. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous.’”

segments.arabic: فرجع بها رسول الله ﷺ يرجف فؤاده فدخل على خديجة بنت خويلد رضى الله تعالى عنها، فقال زملوني زملوني فزملوه حتى ذهب عنه الروع، فقال لخديجة وأخبرها الخبر لقد خشيت على نفسي فقالت خديجة كلا والله ما يخزيك الله أبدا إنك لتصل الرحم وتحمل الكل وتكسب المعدوم وتقري الضيف وتعين على نوائب الحق
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned with it, his heart trembling. He went in to Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, may Allah Most High be pleased with her, and said, “Wrap me up, wrap me up.” They wrapped him up until his fright had left him. He told Khadijah what had happened and said, “I feared for myself.” Khadijah said, “No! By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You maintain ties of kinship, bear the burdens of others, provide for those who have nothing, entertain guests, and help in the adversities that befall people.”

segments.arabic: فانطلقت به خديجة حتى أتت به ورقة بن نوفل بن أسد بن عبد العزى ابن عم خديجة وكان امرأ تنصر في الجاهلية وكان يكتب الكتاب العبراني فيكتب من الإنجيل بالعبرانية ما شاء الله أن يكتب وكان شيخا كبيرا قد عمي فقالت له خديجة يا ابن عم اسمع من ابن أخيك، فقال له ورقة يا ابن أخي ماذا ترى فأخبره رسول الله ﷺ خبر ما رأى،
segments.english: Khadijah took him to Waraqah ibn Nawfal ibn Asad ibn ‘Abd al-‘Uzza, her cousin. He was a man who had become a Christian in the time of ignorance. He used to write the Hebrew script and would write from the Gospel in Hebrew as much as Allah willed him to write. He was an elderly man who had become blind. Khadijah said to him, “Cousin, listen to your nephew.” Waraqah said to him, “Nephew, what do you see?” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, told him what he had seen.

segments.arabic: فقال له ورقة هذا الناموس الذي نزل الله على موسى يا ليتني فيها جذع ليتني أكون حيا إذ يخرجك قومك، فقال رسول الله ﷺ: أو مخرجي هم قال: نعم لم يأت رجل قط بمثل ما جئت به إلا عودي وإن يدركني يومك أنصرك نصرا مؤزرا ثم لم ينشب ورقة أن توفي وفتر الوحي.
segments.english: Waraqah said to him, “This is the Namus whom Allah sent down to Musa. If only I were young then! If only I were alive when your people drive you out!” The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, “Will they drive me out?” He said, “Yes. No man has ever brought the like of what you have brought without being met with hostility. If your day reaches me, I will give you firm support.” Before long, Waraqah died, and revelation paused.

Retains three commands, three replies and three pressings. The selected text states the limit of strength for the first two pressings, not the third. The older print repeats that clause for the third; the modern print agrees with the selected shorter third description. No third limit-of-strength clause is imported.
The quotation ends at al-akram, corresponding to 96:1–3. The draft does not append later verses. Read/cannot-read follows both named translation comparisons; it remains a translation choice.

Retains the repeated wrapping request, fear, five qualities in Khadijah’s reply, Waraqah’s lineage/religion/writing/blindness, question, exile warning, pledge of support, death and pause. Hebrew is retained; no Arabic-writing variant is substituted.

segments.arabic: [4] قال ابن شهاب وأخبرني أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن أن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري قال وهو يحدث عن فترة الوحي، فقال في حديثه
segments.english: Ibn Shihab said: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman also informed me that Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah al-Ansari, speaking about the pause in revelation, said in his account:

segments.arabic: بينا أنا أمشي إذ سمعت صوتا من السماء فرفعت بصري فإذا الملك الذي جاءني بحراء جالس على كرسي بين السماء والأرض فرعبت منه فرجعت فقلت: زملوني زملوني فأنزل الله تعالى { يا أيها المدثر قم فأنذر } إلى قوله { والرجز فاهجر } فحمي الوحي وتتابع
segments.english: “While I was walking, I heard a voice from the sky. I raised my eyes, and there was the angel who had come to me at Hira, sitting on a chair between the sky and the earth. I was frightened of him, so I returned and said, ‘Wrap me up, wrap me up.’ Then Allah Most High sent down: ‘O you wrapped in a cloak, rise and warn,’ up to His words: ‘And shun impurity.’ Revelation then became intense and continued.”

segments.arabic: تابعه عبد الله بن يوسف وأبو صالح وتابعه هلال بن رداد عن الزهري، وقال يونس ومعمر بوادره.
segments.english: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf and Abu Salih followed him in transmitting it. Hilal ibn Raddad also followed him in transmitting it from al-Zuhri. Yunus and Ma‘mar said “bawadiruhu.”

checks.finding: This record starts with Ibn Shihab and continues the preceding chain. The first-person speech is transmitted by Jabir as the Prophet’s account; it must not be presented as Jabir describing his own experience. The abbreviated source does not repeat all upper links or a fresh explicit Prophet attribution.

The selected Arabic explicitly abbreviates the Qur’anic passage with “up to His words”. The draft preserves that abbreviation. Both printed witnesses inspected give intermediate wording; it is not silently filled into this source.

The note beginning taba‘ahu is outside the first-person quotation. The full tail names ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf, Abu Salih, Hilal ibn Raddad, al-Zuhri, Yunus and Ma‘mar. Bewley preserves this note; the Khan-family combined record does not.

segments.arabic: [5] حدثنا موسى بن إسماعيل قال: حدثنا أبو عوانة قال: حدثنا موسى بن أبي عائشة قال: حدثنا سعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى { لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به } قال:
segments.english: Musa ibn Isma‘il related to us: Abu ‘Awanah related to us: Musa ibn Abi ‘A’ishah related to us: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr related to us, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning the words of the Most High, “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.” He said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ يعالج من التنزيل شدة وكان مما يحرك شفتيه، فقال ابن عباس فأنا أحركهما لكم كما كان رسول الله ﷺ يحركهما، وقال سعيد أنا أحركهما كما رأيت ابن عباس يحركهما فحرك شفتيه
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to undergo hardship from the revelation, and he would move his lips. Ibn ‘Abbas said, “I am moving them for you as the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, used to move them.” Sa‘id said, “I am moving them as I saw Ibn ‘Abbas move them,” and he moved his lips.

segments.arabic: فأنزل الله تعالى { لا تحرك به لسانك لتعجل به إن علينا جمعه وقرآنه } قال جمعه له في صدرك وتقرأه { فإذا قرأناه فاتبع قرآنه } قال: فاستمع له وأنصت { ثم إن علينا بيانه } ثم إن علينا أن تقرأه
segments.english: Then Allah Most High sent down: “Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Its collection and recitation are Our responsibility.” He said: “Gathering it for him in your breast, and your reciting it.” “When We recite it, follow its recitation.” He said: “Listen to it and be silent.” “Then its explanation is Our responsibility.” Then it is Our responsibility that you recite it.

segments.arabic: فكان رسول الله ﷺ بعد ذلك إذا أتاه جبريل استمع فإذا انطلق جبريل قرأه النبي ﷺ كما قرأه.
segments.english: After that, when Jibril came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, he would listen. When Jibril departed, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would recite it as he had recited it.

checks.finding: The selected Arabic distinguishes Ibn ‘Abbas’s demonstration and Sa‘id’s later demonstration; both are retained. The older print includes the hardship description and Ibn ‘Abbas’s demonstration. The modern printed page 9 instead moves directly to the Prophet moving them and Sa‘id’s words; its shorter passage is recorded, not used to delete the selected clauses.

The Qur’anic fragments and the transmitted explanations are distinct. The source has lahu in “jam‘ahu lahu fi sadrika”; both inspected printed pages show laka. The draft deliberately exposes the selected source’s “for him … your breast” shift instead of silently repairing it.
Retains listening when Jibril arrived and reciting after he departed. Neither a memorization method nor a separate lesson is added.

segments.arabic: [6] حدثنا عبدان قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا يونس عن الزهري
segments.english: ‘Abdan related to us: ‘Abdullah informed us: Yunus informed us, from al-Zuhri.

segments.arabic: ح وحدثنا بشر بن محمد قال: أخبرنا عبد الله قال: أخبرنا يونس ومعمر عن الزهري نحوه قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله عن ابن عباس قال:
segments.english: Another chain: Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us: ‘Abdullah informed us: Yunus and Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, similarly. He said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah informed me, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said:

segments.arabic: كان رسول الله ﷺ أجود الناس وكان أجود ما يكون في رمضان حين يلقاه جبريل وكان يلقاه في كل ليلة من رمضان فيدارسه القرآن فلرسول الله ﷺ أجود بالخير من الريح المرسلة.
segments.english: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was the most generous of people. He was at his most generous in Ramadan, when Jibril met him. He would meet him every night of Ramadan and study the Qur’an with him. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was more generous in goodness than the wind sent forth.

checks.finding: Retains both ‘Abdan and Bishr routes, Yunus alone in the first and Yunus with Ma‘mar in the second, the similar-wording indication and the transition sign ha. “Another chain” renders the sign’s role and is marked as a chain segment.

Retains the general superlative, Ramadan intensification, every night, reciprocal study of the Qur’an and the wind comparison. Bewley supports a review/study rendering; the Khan-family comparator uses teaching and adds explanatory wording to the wind image. The draft adds no explanation.

segments.arabic: [7] حدثنا أبو اليمان الحكم بن نافع قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: أخبرني عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة بن مسعود أن عبد الله بن عباس أخبره
segments.english: Abu al-Yaman al-Hakam ibn Nafi‘ related to us: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas informed him

segments.arabic: أن أبا سفيان بن حرب أخبره
segments.english: that Abu Sufyan ibn Harb informed him:

segments.arabic: أن هرقل أرسل إليه في ركب من قريش وكانوا تجارا بالشام في المدة التي كان رسول الله ﷺ ماد فيها أبا سفيان وكفار قريش فأتوه وهم بإيلياء فدعاهم في مجلسه وحوله عظماء الروم ثم دعاهم ودعا بترجمانه، فقال أيكم أقرب نسبا بهذا الرجل الذي يزعم أنه نبي، فقال أبو سفيان فقلت: أنا أقربهم نسبا، فقال أدنوه مني وقربوا أصحابه فاجعلوهم عند ظهره، ثم قال لترجمانه قل لهم إني سائل هذا عن هذا الرجل فإن كذبني فكذبوه
segments.english: Heraclius had sent for him among a party of Quraysh who were merchants in al-Sham, during the truce that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, had made with Abu Sufyan and the unbelievers of Quraysh. They came to him while they were in Ilya. He summoned them to his assembly, surrounded by the leading men of the Romans. Then he called them and his interpreter and said, “Which of you is nearest in lineage to this man who claims to be a prophet?” Abu Sufyan said: I replied, “I am nearest to him in lineage.” He said, “Bring him close to me, and bring his companions close and place them behind him.” Then he said to his interpreter, “Tell them that I will question this man about that man. If he lies to me, contradict him.”

segments.arabic: فوالله لولا الحياء من أن يأثروا علي كذبا لكذبت عنه ثم كان أول ما سألني عنه أن قال كيف نسبه فيكم قلت: هو فينا ذو نسب قال: فهل قال هذا القول منكم أحد قط قبله قلت لا قال: فهل كان من آبائه من ملك قلت لا قال: فأشراف الناس يتبعونه أم ضعفاؤهم فقلت: بل ضعفاؤهم قال أيزيدون أم ينقصون قلت: بل يزيدون قال: فهل يرتد أحد منهم سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه قلت لا قال: فهل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول: ما قال: قلت لا قال: فهل يغدر قلت لا ونحن منه في مدة لا ندري ما هو فاعل فيها قال ولم تمكني كلمة أدخل فيها شيئا غير هذه الكلمة
segments.english: By Allah, had I not been ashamed that they would report a lie from me, I would have lied about him. The first thing he asked me was, “What is his lineage among you?” I said, “He is of noble lineage among us.” He said, “Has anyone among you ever said this before him?” I said, “No.” He said, “Was any of his ancestors a king?” I said, “No.” He said, “Do the prominent people follow him, or their weak?” I said, “Their weak.” He said, “Are they increasing or decreasing?” I said, “They are increasing.” He said, “Does anyone turn back in displeasure with his religion after entering it?” I said, “No.” He said, “Did you accuse him of lying before he said what he said?” I said, “No.” He said, “Does he betray?” I said, “No. We are in a truce with him, and we do not know what he will do during it.” He said: I could find no words into which I could insert anything except these.

segments.arabic: قال: فهل قاتلتموه قلت: نعم قال: فكيف كان قتالكم إياه قلت: الحرب بيننا وبينه سجال ينال منا وننال منه قال: ماذا يأمركم قلت: يقول اعبدوا الله وحده ولا تشركوا به شيئا واتركوا ما يقول آباؤكم ويأمرنا بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف والصلة،
segments.english: He said, “Have you fought him?” I said, “Yes.” He said, “How was your fighting against him?” I said, “War between us and him alternates: he gains against us, and we gain against him.” He said, “What does he command you?” I said, “He says: worship Allah alone, associate nothing with Him, and abandon what your forefathers say. He commands us to pray, be truthful, be chaste, and maintain ties of kinship.”

segments.arabic: فقال للترجمان قل له سألتك عن نسبه فذكرت أنه فيكم ذو نسب فكذلك الرسل تبعث في نسب قومها وسألتك هل قال أحد منكم هذا القول فذكرت أن لا فقلت لو كان أحد قال هذا القول قبله لقلت: رجل يأتسي بقول قيل قبله وسألتك هل كان من آبائه من ملك فذكرت أن لا قلت: فلو كان من آبائه من ملك قلت: رجل يطلب ملك أبيه وسألتك هل كنتم تتهمونه بالكذب قبل أن يقول: ما قال: فذكرت أن لا فقد أعرف أنه لم يكن ليذر الكذب على الناس ويكذب على الله
segments.english: He said to the interpreter, “Tell him: I asked you about his lineage, and you said he was of noble lineage among you. Likewise, messengers are sent among the lineages of their peoples. I asked whether anyone among you had said this before, and you said no. Had anyone said it before him, I would have said: a man following words spoken before him. I asked whether any of his ancestors was a king, and you said no. Had one of his ancestors been a king, I would have said: a man seeking his forefather’s kingdom. I asked whether you accused him of lying before he said what he said, and you said no. I know that he would not leave off lying about people and then lie about Allah.

segments.arabic: وسألتك أشراف الناس اتبعوه أم ضعفاؤهم فذكرت أن ضعفاءهم اتبعوه وهم أتباع الرسل وسألتك أيزيدون أم ينقصون فذكرت أنهم يزيدون وكذلك أمر الإيمان حتى يتم وسألتك أيرتد أحد سخطة لدينه بعد أن يدخل فيه فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الإيمان حين تخالط بشاشته القلوب وسألتك هل يغدر فذكرت أن لا وكذلك الرسل لا تغدر
segments.english: “I asked whether the prominent people followed him or their weak, and you said that their weak followed him. They are the followers of the messengers. I asked whether they were increasing or decreasing, and you said they were increasing. Such is the course of faith until it is complete. I asked whether anyone turned back in displeasure with his religion after entering it, and you said no. Such is faith when its joy mingles with hearts. I asked whether he betrayed, and you said no. Likewise, the messengers do not betray.

segments.arabic: وسألتك بما يأمركم فذكرت أنه يأمركم أن تعبدوا الله ولا تشركوا به شيئا وينهاكم عن عبادة الأوثان ويأمركم بالصلاة والصدق والعفاف فإن كان ما تقول حقا فسيملك موضع قدمي هاتين وقد كنت أعلم أنه خارج لم أكن أظن أنه منكم فلو أني أعلم أني أخلص إليه لتجشمت لقاءه ولو كنت عنده لغسلت عن قدمه
segments.english: “I asked what he commanded you, and you said that he commanded you to worship Allah and associate nothing with Him, forbade you to worship idols, and commanded you to pray, be truthful, and be chaste. If what you say is true, he will possess the place beneath these two feet of mine. I knew that he would appear, but I did not think he would be from among you. If I knew that I could reach him, I would undertake the hardship of meeting him. If I were with him, I would wash his foot.”

segments.arabic: ثم دعا بكتاب رسول الله ﷺ الذي بعث به دحية إلى عظيم بصرى فدفعه إلى هرقل فقرأه فإذا فيه
segments.english: Then he called for the letter of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which he had sent with Dihyah to the ruler of Busra, who passed it to Heraclius. He read it, and it contained:

segments.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم من محمد عبد الله ورسوله إلى هرقل عظيم الروم سلام على من اتبع الهدى أما بعد فإني أدعوك بدعاية الإسلام أسلم تسلم يؤتك الله أجرك مرتين فإن توليت فإن عليك إثم الأريسيين و { يا أهل الكتاب تعالوا إلى كلمة سواء بيننا وبينكم أن لا نعبد إلا الله ولا نشرك به شيئا ولا يتخذ بعضنا بعضا أربابا من دون الله فإن تولوا فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون }
segments.english: “In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Merciful. From Muhammad, the servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, ruler of the Romans. Peace be upon whoever follows guidance. To proceed: I call you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam and you will be safe; Allah will grant you your reward twice. If you turn away, you will bear the sin of al-Arisiyyin. And: ‘People of the Scripture, come to a word common to us and you: that we worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and do not take one another as lords apart from Allah. If they turn away, say: bear witness that we are Muslims.’”

segments.arabic: قال أبو سفيان فلما قال: ما قال وفرغ من قراءة الكتاب كثر عنده الصخب وارتفعت الأصوات وأخرجنا فقلت لأصحابي حين أخرجنا لقد أمر أمر بن أبي كبشة إنه يخافه ملك بني الأصفر فما زلت موقنا أنه سيظهر حتى أدخل الله علي الإسلام
segments.english: Abu Sufyan said: When he had said what he said and finished reading the letter, the uproar around him grew and voices rose, and we were sent out. When we were sent out, I said to my companions, “The affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become so great that the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him.” I remained certain that he would prevail until Allah brought Islam to me.

segments.arabic: وكان ابن الناظور صاحب إيلياء وهرقل أسقفا على نصارى الشام يحدث أن هرقل حين قدم إيلياء أصبح يوما خبيث النفس، فقال بعض بطارقته قد استنكرنا هيئتك قال ابن الناظور وكان هرقل حزاء ينظر في النجوم، فقال لهم حين سألوه إني رأيت الليلة حين نظرت في النجوم ملك الختان قد ظهر فمن يختتن من هذه الأمة قالوا ليس يختتن إلا اليهود فلا يهمنك شأنهم واكتب إلى مداين ملكك فيقتلوا من فيهم من اليهود
segments.english: Ibn al-Nazur, the official of Ilya and an associate of Heraclius, was a bishop over the Christians of al-Sham. He used to relate that, when Heraclius came to Ilya, he awoke one day in an ill temper. Some of his dignitaries said, “We find your appearance unusual.” Ibn al-Nazur said: Heraclius was a diviner who studied the stars. When they questioned him, he said, “Last night, when I studied the stars, I saw that the king of the circumcised had appeared. Who among this people is circumcised?” They said, “Only the Jews are circumcised. Do not let their affair concern you. Write to the cities of your kingdom so that they kill the Jews who are in them.”

segments.arabic: فبينما هم على أمرهم أتي هرقل برجل أرسل به ملك غسان يخبر عن خبر رسول الله ﷺ فلما استخبره هرقل قال اذهبوا فانظروا أمختتن هو أم لا فنظروا إليه فحدثوه أنه مختتن وسأله عن العرب، فقال هم يختتنون، فقال هرقل هذا ملك هذه الأمة قد ظهر ثم كتب هرقل إلى صاحب له برومية وكان نظيره في العلم وسار هرقل إلى حمص فلم يرم حمص حتى أتاه كتاب من صاحبه يوافق رأي هرقل على خروج النبي ﷺ وأنه نبي
segments.english: While they were engaged in this matter, a man whom the king of Ghassan had sent with news of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, was brought to Heraclius. After Heraclius questioned him, he said, “Go and see whether he is circumcised or not.” They examined him and told him that he was circumcised. He asked him about the Arabs, and he said, “They are circumcised.” Heraclius said, “The rule of this people has appeared.” Then Heraclius wrote to a companion of his in Rome who was his equal in knowledge. Heraclius travelled to Homs and did not leave Homs until a letter from his companion reached him, agreeing with his view concerning the appearance of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that he was a prophet.

segments.arabic: فأذن هرقل لعظماء الروم في دسكرة له بحمص ثم أمر بأبوابها فغلقت ثم اطلع، فقال: يا معشر الروم هل لكم في الفلاح والرشد وأن يثبت ملككم فتبايعوا هذا النبي فحاصوا حيصة حمر الوحش إلى الأبواب فوجدوها قد غلقت فلما رأى هرقل نفرتهم وأيس من الإيمان قال ردوهم علي، وقال إني قلت: مقالتي آنفا أختبر بها شدتكم على دينكم فقد رأيت فسجدوا له ورضوا عنه فكان ذلك آخر شأن هرقل.
segments.english: Heraclius admitted the leading men of the Romans to an estate of his in Homs. Then he ordered its doors shut and appeared before them. He said, “People of Rome, would you have success and right guidance, and your kingdom remain firm, by pledging allegiance to this Prophet?” They bolted toward the doors like wild asses and found them shut. When Heraclius saw their aversion and despaired of belief, he said, “Bring them back to me.” He said, “I said what I said just now to test your firmness in your religion, and I have seen it.” They prostrated to him and were pleased with him. That was the last of the account of Heraclius.

segments.arabic: رواه صالح بن كيسان ويونس ومعمر عن الزهري.
segments.english: Salih ibn Kaysan, Yunus and Ma‘mar related it from al-Zuhri.

checks.finding: The source ends the first paragraph before Abu Sufyan’s link. Both source paragraphs contribute to the translated chain. No chain link is dropped by treating paragraph two as entirely narration.

Retains the truce, setting/interpreter, companions behind Abu Sufyan, fear of being reported as a liar, all questions and replies, the qualified truce remark, alternating warfare and commands. Weak followers are not narrowed to a financial class in the draft.

The repeated questions in Heraclius’s reply are retained rather than deduplicated. Lineage, prior claim, royal ancestry, truthfulness, followers, increase, apostasy, betrayal and commands remain in order. The selected foot wording is singular; no plural is silently imported.

Retains the route through Dihyah and Busra, the complete letter opening and address, call, doubled reward, warning and the quoted passage corresponding to 3:64. A letter segment is still part of this record, not a new hadith.

Retains Abu Sufyan’s reaction and later Islam, Ibn al-Nazur’s separately introduced account, divination, the reported hostile proposal, the Ghassan messenger, circumcision enquiry, correspondence, Homs, shut doors, flight, retraction and prostration. These are reported actions/words, not app advice. The printed punctuation identifies Ibn al-Nazur as bishop; the English comparisons differ on the surrounding office wording.
The separate source paragraph after the long body is retained in full and remains outside quoted speech. It names Salih ibn Kaysan, Yunus and Ma‘mar transmitting from al-Zuhri.
